Alejandro — thanks for the note and the PO. Looping in Laura (Finance) and Marissa (Payments ops) to confirm.

Summary / options so we can pick the one that works best for you:

1) Preferred: USD SWIFT to our USD nostro (no MXN conversion on Redwood side). If your bank can originate USD by SWIFT, this avoids MXN correspondent deductions entirely. Use the OUR fee option if your bank supports it so the gross USD amount we invoiced arrives at our account.

2) If you must send MXN domestically: we can accept MXN into our Mexican collection account, but note that when MXN is converted to USD (sweep) there is often a correspondent/intermediary bank in the path that may deduct a fixed fee. In that case there are two practical flows:
   - Sender elects OUR: they instruct their bank to pay all intermediary fees so the net credited amount equals the invoice MXN gross. In practice some Mexican rails do not support OUR on local transfers.
   - Sender elects SHA/BEN: intermediary bank fees may be deducted along the path. Redwood's policy is to invoice any shortfall (the amount we expected less the amount received) and we will provide a reconciliation within 48 hours of receipt.

3) Hybrid: send MXN to our local collection account and add a short note to your bank to copy the intermediary clearing (e.g., provide the SWIFT intermediary) — this reduces ambiguity.

I attached a short wire template and an MXN sweep FAQ that explains typical fee ranges and timeline. Laura — can you confirm Redwood's preference on the shortfall handling for this customer? Marissa — can you confirm the intermediary bank Redwood has used recently for MXN sweeps?

Alejandro / Karthik — quick finance note from my side:

- Redwood generally prefers USD SWIFT (option 1) because it guarantees the invoiced USD amount without downstream FX/fee variance. If MediHealth can originate USD, please use the USD instructions in the attached template.
- If MXN is required, please be aware: local MXN -> USD sweeps often route through a US correspondent (most commonly Citibank NY for our MXN clearing) and that correspondent can deduct a flat intermediary fee (usually MXN 200–600 or equivalent in USD).
- If your bank cannot support OUR, select SHA but include a note in the instruction referencing: "Redwood Inference / Inv 8342 — send to Citibank NY intermediary ABA 021000089" (this helps the routing team).
- Redwood policy for customer banks that deduct fees: we will reconcile received vs invoiced and issue a short payment request for any shortfall. We can agree to absorb a one-off small deduction (<USD 15) for partner goodwill, but anything above that will be billed.

I added our Tax ID and VAT breakdown to the invoice (attached). If you want an invoice showing net/gross with a PO number and tax ID on a single line item, let me know and we'll re-issue.

Alejandro / Karthik,

Quick clarification from the payer bank side: domestic MXN transfers inside Mexico do not typically support an "OUR" option when the beneficiary is a foreign entity requiring a foreign correspondent (some local banks will mark OUR but the upstream correspondent may still deduct). If your treasury can originate a SWIFT USD payment from a USD-enabled nostro, that is the cleanest route.

If you must send MXN: please provide the beneficiary CLABE and instruct Bancomex to include the intermediary SWIFT and reference text exactly as provided by Redwood. We will send a SWIFT confirmation (MT103/STA) as soon as the transfer is sent so Redwood can reconcile. Intermediary fees are usually 300–700 MXN depending on the chain.
